questions.q:
If $f: R \rightarrow R$ is defined by f(x)=\left\${\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{\cos 3 x-\cos x}{x^2}, & \text { for } x \neq 0 \\
\lambda & , \text { for } x=0
\end{array}\right. and if $f$ is continuous at $x=0$, then $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that, f(x)=\left\${\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{\cos 3 x-\cos x}{x^2}, & \text { for } x \neq 0 \\
\lambda, & \text { for } x=0
\end{array}\right. Now, \begin{aligned}
\text { LHL } & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x) \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\cos 3 x-\cos x}{x^2} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos 3(0-h)-\cos (0-h)}{(0-h)^2} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos 3 h-\cos h}{h^2} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{-3 \sin 3 h+\sin h}{2 h} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{-9 \cos 3 h+\cos h}{2} \\
& =\frac{-9+1}{2}=-4
\end{aligned} (using L' Hospital's rule)
Since, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$
\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)=f(0) \\
\Rightarrow & -4=\lambda \Rightarrow \lambda=-4
\end{array}

questions.q: If $f(x)=[x]-\left[\frac{x}{4}\right], x \in R$ Where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$, then
options: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)$ exists, but $\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)$ does not exist.
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)$ exists, but $\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)$ does not exist.
Both $\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)$ exist, but are not equal.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)=\left[4^{-}\right]-\left[\frac{4^{-}}{4}\right]=3-0=3 \text { and } \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)=\left[4^{+}\right]-\left[\frac{4^{+}}{4}\right]=4-1=3 \\ & f(4)=[4]-\left[\frac{4}{4}\right]=4-1=3 \\ & \because \lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 4^{+}} f(x)=f(4) \\ & \Rightarrow f(x) ; \text { continuous at } x=4\end{aligned}$

Let,~$n = \dfrac{1}{x}$~so when~$n \to \infty$~then~$x \to 0$.

$∴ y = \lim_{x \to 0}P\left(1 + \dfrac{rx}{100}\right)\dfrac{t}{x}$

Taking log on both sides, we get

$lny = \lim_{x \to 0}lnP\left(1 + \dfrac{rx}{100}\right)\dfrac{t}{x}$

$⇒ lny = lnP + \lim_{x \to $0}t\dfrac{ln\left(1 + \dfrac{rx}{100}\right)}{\dfrac{rx}{100}} \times \dfrac{r}{100}

$⇒ lny - lnP = $\dfrac{rt}{100} \left[$∵ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{ln \left(1 + x\right)}{x} =1\right]$

$⇒ ln\left(\dfrac{y}{P}\right) = \dfrac{rt}{100}$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{P} ==e\dfrac{rt}{100}

$∴ y = Pe\dfrac{rt}{100}

questions.q: If $\quad f:[-2,2] \rightarrow R \quad$ is defined by $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\frac{\sqrt{1+c x}-\sqrt{1-c x}}{x} & \text { for }-2 \leq x < 0 \\ \frac{x+3}{x+1} & \text { for } 0 \leq x \leq 2\end{array}\right.$ continuous on $[-2,2]$, then $c$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $f:[-2,2] \rightarrow R$
f(x)=\left\${\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{\sqrt{1+c x}-\sqrt{1-c x}}{x}, & -2 \leq x < 0 \\
\frac{x+3}{x+1}, & 0 \leq x \leq 2
\end{array}\right. Now, $\quad$ LHL $=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)$
\begin{aligned}
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{1-c h}-\sqrt{1+c h}}{-h} \\
& \times \frac{\sqrt{1-c h}+\sqrt{1+c h}}{\sqrt{1-c h}+\sqrt{1+c h}} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1-c h)-(1+c h)}{-h(\sqrt{1-0}+\sqrt{1+0})} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{-2 c h}{-h(1+1)}=c
\end{aligned} and \mathrm{RHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x) \begin{aligned}
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} f(0+h)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{0+h+3}{0+h+1} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{h+3}{h+1}=\frac{0+3}{0+1}=3
\end{aligned} Since, $f$ is continuous at $x=0$. \therefore \mathrm{LHL}=\mathrm{RHL} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=3

${=e}^{\lim_{z \to 0}\left(\dfrac{p^{z} + q^{z} + r^{z} + s^{z}}{4} - 1\right)\dfrac{3}{z}}$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right)\dfrac{e\dfrac{1}{x} - e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}}{e\dfrac{1}{x} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}}$, where $g$ is a continuous function then $\lim_{x \to 0} ⁡ f  \left(x\right) exists if$

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{e\dfrac{1}{x} - e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}}{e\dfrac{1}{x} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}} = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{1 - e^{- \dfrac{2}{x}}}{1 + e^{- \dfrac{2}{x}}} = 1$

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\dfrac{e\dfrac{1}{x} - e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}}{e\dfrac{1}{x} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}} = \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\dfrac{e\dfrac{2}{x} - 1}{e\dfrac{2}{x} + 1} = - 1$

Hence $\lim_{x \to 0} ⁡ f \left(x\right)$ exists if $g \left(x\right) = xh \left(x\right)$ where $h ( x )$ is a continuous function.

If $g \left($x\right) = a \left($a \ne 0\right)$ then $\lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}f\left($x\right) = a$ and $\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}f \left($x\right) = - a$.

Thus $\lim_{x \to 0} ⁡ $f\left($x\right)$ does not exist if g\left($x\right) = x + 2$ or $x^{4} + 4$ or is a constant function.
